blocks.en: Genesis Intensive — Unit 7: Abraham — Faith, Waiting and the God of the Impossible
blocks.es_reference: Intensivo de Génesis — Unidad 7: Abraham — Fe, Espera y el Dios de lo Imposible

blocks.en: “Is anything too hard for the LORD?” — Genesis 18:14 (NKJV)
blocks.es_reference: “¿Hay para Dios alguna cosa difícil?” — Génesis 18:14 (RVG)

blocks.en: Waiting Tests Faith
blocks.es_reference: La Espera Prueba la Fe

blocks.en: God’s promise to Abraham was clear, but its fulfillment was not immediate. Years passed while Abraham and Sarah remained without the promised son, and the delay exposed the difference between believing a promise and patiently allowing God to fulfill it in His way. Waiting is not empty space in the life of faith. It can reveal fear, impatience, attempts to control outcomes, and the temptation to accomplish by human management what God has promised to provide. Genesis does not present Abraham’s faith as effortless; it shows faith being formed through time.
blocks.es_reference: La promesa de Dios a Abraham era clara, pero su cumplimiento no fue inmediato. Pasaron los años mientras Abraham y Sara seguían sin el hijo prometido, y la demora puso al descubierto la diferencia entre creer una promesa y permitir con paciencia que Dios la cumpla a su manera. La espera no es un espacio vacío en la vida de fe. Puede revelar temor, impaciencia, intentos de controlar los resultados y la tentación de lograr por medios humanos lo que Dios ha prometido proveer. Génesis no presenta la fe de Abraham como algo que no le costara esfuerzo; muestra cómo la fe se va formando con el tiempo.

blocks.en: Hagar and the Attempt to Control the Promise
blocks.es_reference: Agar y el Intento de Controlar la Promesa

blocks.en: Genesis 16 records Sarah’s proposal that Abraham obtain a child through Hagar. The custom belonged to their ancient social world, but the narrative shows the painful consequences of trying to secure the promise through human arrangement. Hagar is not merely a theological object in Abraham’s story; she is a vulnerable woman caught in decisions made by people with greater household power. Once she conceives, rivalry, contempt, and harsh treatment follow. Faith can become distorted when impatience turns another person into an instrument for achieving our desired outcome.
blocks.es_reference: Génesis 16 registra la propuesta de Sara de que Abraham obtenga un hijo por medio de Agar. La costumbre pertenecía a su mundo social antiguo, pero el relato muestra las dolorosas consecuencias de intentar asegurar la promesa mediante arreglos humanos. Agar no es un mero objeto teológico en la historia de Abraham; es una mujer vulnerable, atrapada en decisiones tomadas por personas con más poder dentro de la casa. En cuanto concibe, surgen la rivalidad, el desprecio y el maltrato. La fe puede deformarse cuando la impaciencia convierte a otra persona en un instrumento para lograr el resultado que deseamos.

blocks.en: The God Who Sees Hagar
blocks.es_reference: El Dios que Ve a Agar

blocks.en: Hagar flees into the wilderness, where the angel of the LORD meets her. The episode gives extraordinary attention to a socially vulnerable outsider. God hears her affliction and gives promises concerning Ishmael, and Hagar responds to the God who sees her. The covenant line will run through Isaac, but that does not mean Ishmael or his mother are invisible to God. Genesis can distinguish the particular covenant promise from God’s genuine compassion toward people outside that line.
blocks.es_reference: Agar huye al desierto, donde el ángel de Jehová la encuentra. El episodio presta una atención extraordinaria a una extranjera socialmente vulnerable. Dios oye su aflicción y le da promesas acerca de Ismael, y Agar responde al Dios que la ve. La línea del pacto pasará por Isaac, pero eso no significa que Ismael o su madre sean invisibles para Dios. Génesis puede distinguir entre la promesa particular del pacto y la compasión genuina de Dios hacia personas que están fuera de esa línea.

blocks.en: Ishmael Is Not Forgotten
blocks.es_reference: Ismael No Queda en el Olvido

blocks.en: Ishmael is not the son through whom the specific covenant promise will be established, but Genesis repeatedly refuses to treat him as disposable. God promises to multiply his descendants and later tells Abraham that He has heard his request concerning Ishmael. This distinction matters. Election for a particular redemptive role does not require hostility toward those who do not occupy that role. The God who chooses Isaac for the covenant purpose still hears, sees, and blesses Ishmael.
blocks.es_reference: Ismael no es el hijo por medio de quien se establecerá la promesa específica del pacto, pero Génesis se niega una y otra vez a tratarlo como desechable. Dios promete multiplicar su descendencia y más tarde le dice a Abraham que ha oído su petición acerca de Ismael. Esta distinción importa. Ser elegido para un papel redentor particular no exige hostilidad hacia quienes no ocupan ese papel. El Dios que escoge a Isaac para el propósito del pacto sigue oyendo, viendo y bendiciendo a Ismael.

blocks.en: El Shaddai and the Renewed Covenant
blocks.es_reference: El Shaddai y el Pacto Renovado

blocks.en: When Abram is ninety-nine, Genesis 17 opens with God identifying Himself as God Almighty, El Shaddai, and reaffirming the covenant. The title appropriately emphasizes divine sufficiency and power in a situation where human capacity has reached its limit. Yet omnipotence should not be converted into a promise that God will perform every extraordinary outcome a believer desires. God’s power serves God’s character and purpose. In Abraham’s story the impossible birth is certain because God has specifically promised it.
blocks.es_reference: Cuando Abram tiene noventa y nueve años, Génesis 17 comienza con Dios identificándose como Dios Todopoderoso, El Shaddai, y reafirmando el pacto. Con razón el título destaca la suficiencia y el poder divinos en una situación en la que la capacidad humana ha llegado a su límite. Sin embargo, la omnipotencia no debe convertirse en la promesa de que Dios realizará cualquier resultado extraordinario que un creyente desee. El poder de Dios está al servicio de su carácter y de su propósito. En la historia de Abraham, el nacimiento imposible es seguro porque Dios lo ha prometido expresamente.

blocks.en: New Names and Covenant Identity
blocks.es_reference: Nuevos Nombres e Identidad del Pacto

blocks.en: God changes Abram’s name to Abraham and Sarai’s name to Sarah as the promise is reaffirmed. The new names are connected with the future God is creating: Abraham will be father of many nations, and Sarah will become mother within the promised line. Biblical naming can mark identity and calling, but the point here is not a technique by which believers rename themselves into a preferred destiny. God is the speaker and covenant maker. Their identity is being shaped by His promise rather than by self-invention.
blocks.es_reference: Dios cambia el nombre de Abram a Abraham, y el de Sarai a Sara, al reafirmar la promesa. Los nuevos nombres están ligados al futuro que Dios está creando: Abraham será padre de muchas naciones, y Sara llegará a ser madre dentro de la línea prometida. En la Biblia, poner un nombre puede señalar la identidad y el llamamiento, pero aquí no se trata de una técnica con la que los creyentes se pongan un nombre nuevo para alcanzar el destino que prefieren. Quien habla y hace el pacto es Dios. La identidad de ellos se forma por la promesa de Él, no por invención propia.

blocks.en: Laughter at the Impossible
blocks.es_reference: Risa ante lo Imposible

blocks.en: Both Abraham and Sarah respond with laughter when confronted with the prospect of a son in their old age. Their laughter carries the tension between promise and visible impossibility. Genesis does not require us to pretend that faith never feels the weight of circumstances. The promised birth is humanly beyond expectation, and that is precisely why its fulfillment will display divine faithfulness. Isaac’s name, associated with laughter, will preserve the memory that God fulfilled what appeared impossible.
blocks.es_reference: Tanto Abraham como Sara responden con risa ante la perspectiva de tener un hijo en su vejez. Su risa encierra la tensión entre la promesa y la imposibilidad visible. Génesis no nos exige fingir que la fe nunca siente el peso de las circunstancias. Humanamente, el nacimiento prometido supera toda expectativa, y precisamente por eso su cumplimiento mostrará la fidelidad divina. El nombre Isaac, asociado con la risa, preservará la memoria de que Dios cumplió lo que parecía imposible.

blocks.en: “Is Anything Too Hard for the LORD?”
blocks.es_reference: «¿Hay para Dios Alguna Cosa Difícil?»

blocks.en: Genesis 18:14 asks the question that stands over this stage of Abraham’s life: “Is anything too hard for the LORD?” In context, the question is tied directly to God’s announced return and Sarah’s promised son. It therefore teaches more than optimism but less than a blank check for every human wish. Nothing God purposes and promises is beyond His ability to accomplish. Faith rests not in the supposed power of positive expectation but in the power and faithfulness of the LORD.
blocks.es_reference: Génesis 18:14 hace la pregunta que domina esta etapa de la vida de Abraham: «¿Hay para Dios alguna cosa difícil?» En su contexto, la pregunta está ligada directamente al regreso que Dios anuncia y al hijo prometido a Sara. Por eso enseña más que un simple optimismo, pero menos que un cheque en blanco para cualquier deseo humano. Nada de lo que Dios se propone y promete está fuera de su capacidad de realizarlo. La fe no descansa en el supuesto poder de las expectativas positivas, sino en el poder y la fidelidad de Jehová.

blocks.en: Abraham’s Intercession
blocks.es_reference: La Intercesión de Abraham

blocks.en: Genesis 18 then turns from promised life to threatened judgment as Abraham intercedes concerning Sodom. Abraham’s prayer is bold yet reverent: “Shall not the Judge of all the earth do right?” He appeals to God’s justice rather than placing himself above God as moral judge. The passage gives ministers a model of serious intercession for people facing judgment while maintaining confidence in divine righteousness. Compassion and holiness need not be enemies.
blocks.es_reference: Génesis 18 pasa luego de la vida prometida al juicio que amenaza, mientras Abraham intercede por Sodoma. La oración de Abraham es audaz pero reverente: «El Juez de toda la tierra, ¿no ha de hacer lo que es justo?» Apela a la justicia de Dios en vez de colocarse por encima de Dios como juez moral. El pasaje ofrece a los ministros un modelo de intercesión seria por las personas que enfrentan el juicio, sin perder la confianza en la justicia divina. La compasión y la santidad no tienen por qué ser enemigas.

blocks.en: The Sin and Judgment of Sodom
blocks.es_reference: El Pecado y el Juicio de Sodoma

blocks.en: Genesis 19 depicts a city marked by grave corruption, including threatened sexual violence against vulnerable visitors. Later biblical references also associate Sodom with arrogance, abundance without care for the poor, and other forms of wickedness. Responsible teaching should neither minimize the sexual violence in Genesis 19 nor reduce every biblical reference to Sodom to a single sin while ignoring the wider portrait of corruption. The chapter presents holy judgment upon a deeply disordered society. It also warns that prosperity and social confidence cannot shield a culture from moral accountability before God.
blocks.es_reference: Génesis 19 presenta una ciudad marcada por una grave corrupción, que incluye la amenaza de violencia sexual contra visitantes vulnerables. Referencias bíblicas posteriores también asocian a Sodoma con la arrogancia, con la abundancia sin cuidado del pobre y con otras formas de maldad. Una enseñanza responsable no debe minimizar la violencia sexual de Génesis 19 ni reducir toda referencia bíblica a Sodoma a un solo pecado, pasando por alto el cuadro más amplio de su corrupción. El capítulo presenta un juicio santo sobre una sociedad profundamente desordenada. También advierte que la prosperidad y la confianza social no pueden librar a una cultura de rendir cuentas moralmente delante de Dios.

blocks.en: Lot — Righteous Yet Compromised
blocks.es_reference: Lot — Justo, pero Transigente

blocks.en: The New Testament calls Lot righteous, which prevents us from dismissing him as simply an unbeliever. Genesis nevertheless portrays a man whose choices have placed him and his family in a morally dangerous setting and whose influence appears tragically limited. His story is therefore more sobering than a simple label. A person may genuinely belong to God and still make choices that expose a household to destructive influences. Grace does not make wisdom unnecessary.
blocks.es_reference: El Nuevo Testamento llama justo a Lot, lo cual nos impide descartarlo sin más como un incrédulo. Sin embargo, Génesis presenta a un hombre cuyas decisiones lo han colocado a él y a su familia en un ambiente moralmente peligroso, y cuya influencia parece trágicamente limitada. Por eso su historia es más aleccionadora que una simple etiqueta. Una persona puede pertenecer genuinamente a Dios y aun así tomar decisiones que expongan a su familia a influencias destructivas. La gracia no hace innecesaria la sabiduría.

blocks.en: Mercy in the Midst of Judgment
blocks.es_reference: Misericordia en Medio del Juicio

blocks.en: Genesis 19 says that the angels took Lot and his family by the hand because the LORD was merciful to him. Even in a judgment narrative, deliverance is described in the language of mercy. Lot’s rescue is not an endorsement of every decision he has made. It is another reminder that the human characters of Genesis survive by divine mercy rather than by presenting flawless records. Holy judgment and undeserved mercy stand beside one another.
blocks.es_reference: Génesis 19 dice que los ángeles tomaron de la mano a Lot y a su familia porque Jehová tuvo misericordia de él. Aun en un relato de juicio, la liberación se describe en términos de misericordia. El rescate de Lot no es una aprobación de todas las decisiones que ha tomado. Es otro recordatorio de que los personajes humanos de Génesis sobreviven por la misericordia divina, no por presentar un historial intachable. El juicio santo y la misericordia inmerecida aparecen uno junto al otro.

blocks.en: Abraham Repeats an Old Failure
blocks.es_reference: Abraham Repite un Viejo Fracaso

blocks.en: Genesis 20 records another episode in which Abraham identifies Sarah as his sister and fear again produces deception. The repetition is spiritually important because growth is real without always being linear. A believer can revisit an old weakness after genuine experiences of God. Abimelech’s response also prevents Abraham from occupying the easy position of morally superior insider. God protects the promise, but Abraham is still responsible for conduct that endangered others.
blocks.es_reference: Génesis 20 registra otro episodio en el que Abraham presenta a Sara como su hermana, y el temor vuelve a producir engaño. La repetición es espiritualmente importante porque el crecimiento es real aunque no siempre sea lineal. Un creyente puede recaer en una antigua debilidad después de haber tenido experiencias genuinas con Dios. La respuesta de Abimelec también impide que Abraham ocupe la cómoda posición de quien, por estar dentro, se considera moralmente superior. Dios protege la promesa, pero Abraham sigue siendo responsable de una conducta que puso en peligro a otros.

blocks.en: The Promised Son Arrives
blocks.es_reference: Llega el Hijo Prometido

blocks.en: Genesis 21 opens with emphatic language: the LORD visited Sarah “as He had said,” and did for Sarah “as He had spoken.” Isaac’s birth is therefore first a testimony to the faithfulness of God. The long delay, human schemes, laughter, and repeated failures have not canceled the promise. Sarah’s laughter is transformed into astonished joy. The point is not that every delayed desire will eventually be granted, but that God is faithful to what He has actually promised.
blocks.es_reference: Génesis 21 comienza con un lenguaje enfático: Jehová visitó a Sara «como había dicho» e hizo con Sara «como había hablado». Por tanto, el nacimiento de Isaac es, ante todo, un testimonio de la fidelidad de Dios. La larga demora, las maquinaciones humanas, la risa y los fracasos repetidos no han anulado la promesa. La risa de Sara se transforma en un gozo lleno de asombro. No se trata de que todo deseo postergado vaya a concederse tarde o temprano, sino de que Dios es fiel a lo que realmente ha prometido.

blocks.en: Hagar and Ishmael in the Wilderness
blocks.es_reference: Agar e Ismael en el Desierto

blocks.en: Conflict in Abraham’s household eventually leads to Hagar and Ishmael being sent away, a painful scene that must not be treated casually. In the wilderness their water is exhausted and Hagar fears the death of her son. God hears the boy, speaks reassurance, opens Hagar’s eyes to water, and remains with Ishmael as he grows. The covenant promise through Isaac remains distinct, but divine compassion reaches Hagar and Ishmael again. The God of Abraham is also the God who hears the cry of the vulnerable.
blocks.es_reference: Con el tiempo, el conflicto en la casa de Abraham lleva a que Agar e Ismael sean despedidos, una escena dolorosa que no debe tratarse a la ligera. En el desierto se les acaba el agua, y Agar teme que su hijo muera. Dios oye al muchacho, da palabras de aliento, abre los ojos de Agar para que vea el agua y permanece con Ismael mientras crece. La promesa del pacto por medio de Isaac sigue siendo distinta, pero la compasión divina alcanza de nuevo a Agar y a Ismael. El Dios de Abraham es también el Dios que oye el clamor de los vulnerables.

blocks.en: Promise and Consequences
blocks.es_reference: Promesa y Consecuencias

blocks.en: God’s faithfulness does not erase every consequence of Abraham and Sarah’s earlier attempt to manage the promise. Their household experiences rivalry, grief, and separation. Forgiveness and grace are real, but Scripture does not teach that every temporal consequence disappears when sin is forgiven. This distinction is pastorally important. People need hope that grace restores relationship with God without being promised that all damaged circumstances will instantly return to what they were before.
blocks.es_reference: La fidelidad de Dios no borra todas las consecuencias del intento anterior de Abraham y Sara de manejar la promesa. Su casa sufre rivalidad, dolor y separación. El perdón y la gracia son reales, pero la Escritura no enseña que toda consecuencia temporal desaparezca cuando el pecado es perdonado. Esta distinción es importante en lo pastoral. Las personas necesitan la esperanza de que la gracia restaura la relación con Dios, sin que se les prometa que toda circunstancia dañada volverá al instante a ser como antes.

blocks.en: Faith Learns to Release Control
blocks.es_reference: La Fe Aprende a Soltar el Control

blocks.en: Across Genesis 16–21, one recurring lesson is the inadequacy of human control. Abraham and Sarah cannot manufacture the covenant heir by their own arrangement, cannot make the impossible possible through effort, and cannot preserve the promise through deception. Yet they are not passive spectators. They must listen, obey, intercede, repent, care, and respond. Biblical trust is neither anxious control nor fatalistic inactivity; it is responsible action under confidence in the God whose promise does not depend upon our manipulation.
blocks.es_reference: A lo largo de Génesis 16–21, una lección que se repite es la insuficiencia del control humano. Abraham y Sara no pueden fabricar al heredero del pacto con sus propios arreglos, ni hacer posible lo imposible con su esfuerzo, ni preservar la promesa mediante el engaño. Sin embargo, no son espectadores pasivos. Deben escuchar, obedecer, interceder, arrepentirse, cuidar y responder. La confianza bíblica no es control ansioso ni inactividad fatalista; es acción responsable, sostenida por la confianza en el Dios cuya promesa no depende de nuestra manipulación.

blocks.en: The God of the Impossible
blocks.es_reference: El Dios de lo Imposible

blocks.en: The question of Genesis 18:14 reaches beyond Sarah’s pregnancy because it reveals something fundamental about God: human limitation does not limit Him. Yet the safest and strongest application is anchored in His revealed promises. Christians do not know that every illness will be cured now, every broken relationship restored, every financial crisis reversed, or every desired door opened. They do know that God is able to accomplish His redemptive purpose, sustain His people, give wisdom and grace, raise the dead, and complete what He has promised in Christ. Biblical confidence is therefore stronger than wishful thinking because its object is God Himself.
blocks.es_reference: La pregunta de Génesis 18:14 va más allá del embarazo de Sara, porque revela algo fundamental acerca de Dios: las limitaciones humanas no lo limitan a Él. Sin embargo, la aplicación más segura y más firme está anclada en sus promesas reveladas. Los cristianos no tienen la certeza de que toda enfermedad vaya a sanarse ahora, de que toda relación rota vaya a restaurarse, de que toda crisis financiera vaya a revertirse ni de que toda puerta deseada vaya a abrirse. Lo que sí saben es que Dios puede cumplir su propósito redentor, sostener a su pueblo, dar sabiduría y gracia, resucitar a los muertos y completar lo que ha prometido en Cristo. Por eso la confianza bíblica es más fuerte que las meras ilusiones, porque su objeto es Dios mismo.

blocks.en: Ministry Application
blocks.es_reference: Aplicación Ministerial

blocks.en: People in ministry often live between promise and fulfillment. That space can tempt leaders to manipulate outcomes, use people instrumentally, exaggerate certainty, or call personal ambition a divine promise. Abraham’s story warns against those shortcuts while giving profound encouragement. God sees vulnerable people, remains faithful despite human weakness, welcomes intercession, judges evil, and accomplishes what He has actually promised. Mature ministry learns to wait without becoming passive, act without trying to control God, and hope without promising people miracles that Scripture has not promised them.
blocks.es_reference: Quienes están en el ministerio a menudo viven entre la promesa y su cumplimiento. Ese espacio puede tentar a los líderes a manipular los resultados, usar a las personas como instrumentos, exagerar su certeza o llamar promesa divina a su ambición personal. La historia de Abraham advierte contra esos atajos, a la vez que da un profundo ánimo. Dios ve a las personas vulnerables, permanece fiel a pesar de la debilidad humana, acoge la intercesión, juzga el mal y cumple lo que realmente ha prometido. El ministerio maduro aprende a esperar sin volverse pasivo, a actuar sin intentar controlar a Dios y a tener esperanza sin prometer a las personas milagros que la Escritura no les ha prometido.

blocks.en: Summary
blocks.es_reference: Resumen

blocks.en: Genesis 16–21 shows Abraham and Sarah learning that the promise belongs to God. Human impatience produces painful consequences through Hagar, yet God sees Hagar and hears Ishmael. God Almighty reaffirms the covenant, gives new names, answers skeptical laughter, invites intercession, judges Sodom, shows mercy to Lot, protects Sarah despite Abraham’s repeated fear, and finally gives Isaac exactly as He said. The central lesson is not that faithful people always receive the impossible outcome they desire. It is that nothing God purposes and promises is too hard for the LORD.
blocks.es_reference: Génesis 16–21 muestra a Abraham y Sara aprendiendo que la promesa pertenece a Dios. La impaciencia humana produce consecuencias dolorosas por medio de Agar, pero Dios ve a Agar y oye a Ismael. El Dios Todopoderoso reafirma el pacto, da nombres nuevos, responde a la risa escéptica, invita a la intercesión, juzga a Sodoma, muestra misericordia a Lot, protege a Sara a pesar del temor repetido de Abraham y, por fin, da a Isaac exactamente como lo dijo. La lección central no es que las personas fieles siempre reciban el resultado imposible que desean. Es que nada de lo que Dios se propone y promete es demasiado difícil para Jehová.

mc.stem: What problem does waiting expose in Abraham and Sarah?
options: The temptation to return to their homeland in Ur
The temptation to control how God’s promise will be fulfilled
The temptation to give up on having an heir at all
The temptation to worship the gods of Canaan instead
mc.why: The temptation to control how God’s promise will be fulfilled.

mc.stem: How should Hagar be treated in the narrative?
options: As an outsider God ignores because she is not chosen
As a vulnerable person whom God sees and hears
As the mother through whom the covenant continues
As a mere instrument in Abraham’s story
mc.why: As a vulnerable person whom God sees and hears.

mc.stem: Through whom will the specific covenant line continue?
options: Lot
Eliezer
Isaac
Ishmael
mc.why: Isaac.

mc.stem: Does that covenant distinction mean God abandons Ishmael?
options: No; God hears and blesses him
Yes; he is cut off from all blessing
No; he replaces Isaac as covenant heir
Yes; God turns away from him entirely
mc.why: No; God hears and blesses him.

mc.stem: What title does God use in Genesis 17?
options: The God Who Sees, El Roi
God Most High, El Elyon
God Almighty, El Shaddai
The Everlasting God, El Olam
mc.why: God Almighty, El Shaddai.

mc.stem: What do the new names Abraham and Sarah emphasize?
options: Identity shaped by God’s covenant promise
Identity chosen by Abraham and Sarah themselves
Adoption of the customs of Canaan
Honor earned by Abraham’s victory over the kings
mc.why: Identity shaped by God’s covenant promise.

mc.stem: What reaction accompanies the promised birth announcement?
options: Weeping
Silence
Anger
Laughter
mc.why: Laughter.

mc.stem: In context, what does Genesis 18:14 affirm?
options: God can accomplish what He has promised
Abraham’s faith can accomplish the impossible
Positive expectation can make anything happen
God will grant whatever believers desire
mc.why: God can accomplish what He has promised.

mc.stem: What does Abraham appeal to in his intercession for Sodom?
options: The justice of the Judge of all the earth
The wealth and importance of Sodom
The treaty he made with the king of Sodom
His own standing as a righteous man
mc.why: The justice of the Judge of all the earth.

mc.stem: What corruption is explicit in Genesis 19?
options: Rebellion against the rule of the eastern kings
Harsh treatment of Hagar and her son
Worship of idols at a pagan temple
Threatened sexual violence among wider wickedness
mc.why: Threatened sexual violence among wider wickedness.

mc.stem: How does the New Testament describe Lot?
options: Wicked
Lawless
Unbelieving
Righteous
mc.why: Righteous.

mc.stem: Why is Lot rescued?
options: The LORD is merciful to him
His wife urges him to flee
He wins over the men of Sodom
He has lived without fault
mc.why: The LORD is merciful to him.

mc.stem: What old weakness does Abraham repeat in Genesis 20?
options: Mocking laughter at God’s promise
Fearful deception concerning Sarah
Quarreling with Lot over land
Impatient reliance on Hagar
mc.why: Fearful deception concerning Sarah.

mc.stem: What does Genesis 21 emphasize about Isaac’s birth?
options: The birth came later than God had said
Abraham earned the son by his obedience
The LORD did exactly as He had spoken
Sarah conceived through her own planning
mc.why: The LORD did exactly as He had spoken.

mc.stem: What happens to Hagar and Ishmael in Genesis 21?
options: Abraham sends servants to bring them home
Sarah relents and invites them back
They return to Egypt and are forgotten
God hears them and provides in the wilderness
mc.why: God hears them and provides in the wilderness.

mc.stem: Does forgiveness necessarily remove every temporal consequence?
options: Only for small sins
Yes
No
Yes, if repentance is sincere
mc.why: No.

mc.stem: What does Abraham’s story reject as a model of faith?
options: Patient trust in God’s timing
Bold intercession for others
Anxious manipulation of outcomes
Repentance after failure
mc.why: Anxious manipulation of outcomes.

mc.stem: What does biblical trust combine?
options: Anxious control with personal effort
Positive thinking with careful planning
Fatalistic waiting without any action
Responsible action with confidence in God
mc.why: Responsible action with confidence in God.

mc.stem: Does “nothing is too hard for God” promise every desired miracle?
options: No; it applied only to Sarah and says nothing about God
No; it assures God’s ability to fulfill His purposes and promises
Yes; it guarantees every miracle a believer asks for in faith
Yes; strong enough expectation will bring any desired outcome
mc.why: No; it assures God’s ability to fulfill His purposes and promises.

mc.stem: Who remains central throughout Genesis 16–21?
options: Sarah, the patient and faithful mother
The faithful, holy, and powerful God
Abraham, the flawless hero of faith
Lot, the righteous man of Sodom
mc.why: The faithful, holy, and powerful God.
